chunks: Looking at the Kaaba is an act of worship, looking at one’s parents is an act of worship, looking into the muṣḥaf without recitation is an act of worship, looking at the face of the scholar is an act of worship, and looking at the family of Muḥammad, peace be upon them, is an act of worship.

key_terms.آلِ مُحَمَّدٍ: the family of Muḥammad صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم
key_terms.الْعَالِمِ: the scholar, a person of sacred knowledge
key_terms.الْكَعْبَةِ: the Kaaba, the sacred House of Allah
key_terms.عِبَادَةٌ: an act of worship and devotion

ai.seo_question: What kinds of looking are considered acts of worship in Islam?
ai.summary: This hadith teaches that worship is not limited to formal rituals, but also includes reverent looking at sacred and honored realities. It highlights the spiritual merit of the Kaaba, parents, the Qur'an, the scholar, and Āl Muḥammad عليهم السلام.
